title: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting - Cultural and Creative Arts - Painting
exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: A painting composed entirely of inanimate, non-living, and immovable objects arranged on a table is known as:
questions.explain: Still life painting features natural or man-made inanimate objects—such as fruits, flowers in a vase, bottles, and pots—arranged in a specific way by the artist.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: Which of the following painting categories focuses on depicting outdoor sceneries like mountains, valleys, rivers, and forests?
questions.explain: Landscape painting is the depiction of natural scenery such as mountains, valleys, trees, rivers, and forests, typically where the main subject is a wide view with its elements arranged into a coherent composition.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: An artwork titled 'The Market Square from my Dream' which the artist painted strictly from memory and personal fantasy without looking at a physical scene is an example of:
questions.explain: Imaginative painting is derived entirely from the artist's mind, memories, or dreams, rather than through direct observation of the physical world.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: A figure painting primarily involves the artistic representation of:
questions.explain: Figure painting, also closely related to life painting, focuses specifically on observing and rendering the human form in various postures and lighting.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: Nature painting is closely related to landscape painting, but specifically places heavy emphasis on the detailed study of:
options: Busy modern city streets and skyscrapers.
Plants, animals, birds, and other organic environmental elements.
questions.explain: While landscapes capture broad outdoor views, nature painting often hones in on the specific details of flora, fauna, and botanical elements in their natural state.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: In the context of painting techniques, 'tone' refers to:
options: The roughness or smoothness of the canvas.
The lightness or darkness of a color.
The speed at which the paint dries.
The specific type of brush used.
questions.explain: Tone (or value) is an element of art that defines how light or dark a color is. It helps create the illusion of form and 3D depth in a flat painting.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: To create a 'tint' of blue paint, an artist must mix blue with which of the following colors?
questions.explain: A tint is a lighter variation of a color, which is achieved in painting by adding white to the pure color pigment.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: Conversely, if an artist adds black to a pure color in order to make it darker and represent shadows, they have created a:
questions.explain: A shade is the opposite of a tint; it is produced by adding black to a color to decrease its lightness, often used for painting shadows.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: Which basic visual element is created when a line encloses a space on the canvas?
questions.explain: A shape is a two-dimensional, flat, enclosed area created when a line connects to itself or intersects with other lines.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: Which grouping of subjects would perfectly constitute a traditional Still Life composition for a BECE practical exam?
options: A flowing river, an old bridge, and distant hills.
A clay pot, three oranges, and a folded piece of Ankara cloth on a table.
A portrait of the school principal sitting on a chair.
A marketplace with people buying and selling.
questions.explain: The clay pot, oranges, and cloth are all inanimate, stationary objects arranged on a table, strictly fitting the definition of a still life composition.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: When rendering a figure painting, the artist carefully uses variations of tones to create the illusion of solidity. This technique of blending light and dark is often called:
questions.explain: Using tones (lights and shadows) to give flat shapes a 3-dimensional, solid appearance is known as shading or modeling in 2D art.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: A student tasked with painting an imaginative composition is expected to heavily rely on:
options: A photograph given by the teacher.
The physical objects placed directly in front of the class.
Their creative memory, inner vision, and conceptual ideas.
A transparent tracing paper placed over a textbook image.
questions.explain: Imaginative composition tests a student's ability to conceptualize and visualize a scene using their brain's memory and creativity without physical references.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
